misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program HitungUmurAnjing
kamus
  umur, tahunTerhitung : integer
  umurAnjing : real
algoritma
  input(umur)
  umurAnjing <- 0
  tahunTerhitung <- 0
  if tahunTerhitung < 2 and tahunTerhitung < umur then
    umurAnjing <- umurAnjing + 10.5
    tahunTerhitung <- tahunTerhitung + 1
  endif
  if tahunTerhitung < umur then
    umurAnjing <- umurAnjing + 4
    tahunTerhitung <- tahunTerhitung + 1
  endif
  output(umurAnjing)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student rewrote the solution using if-statements with counters, genuinely believing that the if-statements would execute repeatedly as long as their conditions remain true (like while loops). They expect the first if-statement to loop and add 10.5 for each of the first 2 years, then the second if-statement to loop and add 4 for each remaining year. In reality, each if-statement executes at most once, so for a dog older than 2 years, this code would return 14.5 (10.5 + 4) instead of the correct value. For example, a 5-year-old dog should be 33 in dog years, but this code returns 14.5.
